correctness.rationale: The corrected RESULT.md under repairs/5 retains the mathematical claim, corrects the earlier attribution, and supplies explicit smoothness and jet-separation arguments in place of compressed steps. At a fixed base point the row of base monomials provides the quotient to O(3), and the displayed matrix spans its kernel, so after a splitting the quadric equation and three auxiliary quadrics vary independently. Off the fixed line, Q and the three tangential derivatives plus value of C give five total conditions for a critical point over a five-dimensional test space; arbitrary quadratic terms with vanishing first jet allow a further Hessian condition. The incidents with dQ=0 have codimension six off the line and five on it. On the line, proportionality of dC to dQ adds three conditions beyond Q=0, including the conormal case. The universal total incidence off the line is a vector bundle over the smooth test space, so generic smoothness in characteristic zero makes the general total threefold smooth there; independence of the vertical derivatives handles the line. At a node this forces a transverse parameter derivative and gives the Morse local model. For two distinct off-line critical points, independent evaluation vectors of the linear forms let one multiply a linear combination vanishing at one point by a quadric also vanishing there; an adjusting square gives arbitrary first jet at the other point without introducing a jet at the first. In the proportional case the test-pair locus loses two dimensions and the nine-dimensional image of two ambient quadric jets loses at most two on tangent restriction. Thus the independent-vector case has codimension 10 over dimension 9, and the proportional case at least 9 over dimension 7. Fiber complete intersections are connected and S2 with isolated nodes, hence normal and irreducible. Independently, the original ambient divisor classes 3a+2b and −a+3b give [X]=7ab+6b² and c₃(TX)=−3ab²−10b³ from the Newton power sum and c₁=0. Integration gives −88 without requiring the flop or Hodge data; the alternate flop calculation also gives −88. A smooth fiber has Euler characteristic 24; one ordinary double point lowers it to 23. Distinct Morse critical values then give 136 fibers, a simple discriminant at each, and Picard–Lefschetz reflections. No uploaded script was executed.
residual_risks: Only general complex parameters are covered. Euler arithmetic, including the independently replayed flop calculation, would count total node contributions but cannot on its own prove the distinct critical values or the reduced discriminant.
